title: Faithful birational left translations of a strict law
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subset Y$ in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for every $s\in S$. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, modulo agreement on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Smoothness and finite type have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A strict birational law on a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme $Y$ with nonempty fibres is an associative $S$-rational map $m:Y\times_SY\dashrightarrow Y$ for which there are opens $D,V,W\subset Y\times_SY$, each dense in every fibre of both projections to $Y$, such that $m$ is defined on $D$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$, $(x,y)\mapsto(m(x,y),y)$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$ and $D\simeq W$, respectively. Let $Y$ carry such a strict law $m$. For an $S$-scheme $T$, put $Y_T=Y\times_ST$ and let $B_Y(T)$ be the group, under composition, of $T$-birational self-maps of $Y_T$. Pullback defines a contravariant group-valued functor $B_Y$ on $S$-schemes. Here a $T$-birational self-map is an isomorphism between $T$-dense opens modulo agreement on a $T$-dense common open. For $a\in Y(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(T,Y)$, pull back the universal left translation $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$ along $a$ in its first coordinate, obtaining $\tau_a\in B_Y(T)$. These assignments give an injective map $Y(T)\to B_Y(T)$ for every $T$, natural in $T$. If $(a,b)\in Y(T)^2$ factors through any open on which the rational law $m$ is represented by a morphism, then $\tau_{m(a,b)}=\tau_a\circ\tau_b$. These assertions include nonreduced $T$ and arbitrary $T\to S$.

source.place: 5.2 Lemma 4 and its preceding construction, printed pp.118-119 (PDF pp.124-125); primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf, local PDF WANTED

proof.text: First construct the group functor, without any translation law. By [lem-sfb-strict-law-base-change], $Y_T$ is smooth, separated, finite type, with nonempty fibres for every $T\to S$. The density assertion of [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] implies that inverse images of fibrewise dense opens under further base change remain fibrewise dense. Finite intersections of dense opens in each fibre are dense. If $f:U\simeq V$ and $g:U'\simeq V'$ represent two birational self-maps, restrict $f$ to $U\cap f^{-1}(V\cap U')$ and compose with $g$; this is an isomorphism onto an open dense in every fibre, since $V\cap U'$ is dense in $V$ and the restriction is an isomorphism. Equivalent representatives give the same composite after intersecting the finitely many relevant dense opens. The identity of $Y_T$, reversed isomorphisms, and associativity of morphism composition give the group axioms. Pullback carries these representatives, intersections, composites and inverses to the corresponding ones over $T'$. The fibre-product universal property identifies successive pullbacks with direct pullback; hence the induced maps on equivalence classes obey the identity and composition laws. This constructs $B_Y$ on arbitrary test schemes.

source.place: 5.2, construction immediately before Lemma 4, printed p.118; 2.5 on base change of dense opens

proof.text: Write $L:D\simeq V$ for $(x,y)\mapsto(x,m(x,y))$. The projection $Y\times_SY\to Y$ is smooth: apply [lem-sfb-strict-law-base-change] to $Y\to S$ and the base $Y$. Its opens $D,V$ are dense in every fibre by strictness. Pulling $L$ back along any $a:T\to Y$ gives an isomorphism $D_a\simeq V_a$ of $T$-dense opens of $Y_T$ by [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change]. This defines $\tau_a$. A different representative of the rational multiplication agrees on a fibrewise dense common open; schematic density and the closed diagonal of $Y$ extend that agreement to the intersection of its domain with $D$ (the equalizer ideal restricts to zero, so injectivity into the open's structure sheaf makes it zero). For that equalizer argument, the common domain is smooth over $S$: the double product is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition], and its open domain is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Thus the construction uses the rational law itself. Pullback along $T'\to T$ gives exactly $D_{a|T'}\simeq V_{a|T'}$, so $\tau$ is natural.

source.place: 5.2 preceding construction of the universal left translation, printed p.118

proof.text: Suppose $\tau_a=\tau_b$ in $B_Y(T)$. Choose a $T$-dense common open $H$ where their representatives agree, and intersect it with $D_a$ and $D_b$; this is still $T$-dense. Let $R:D\simeq W$ be the other strictness isomorphism, $R(x,y)=(m(x,y),y)$. The two maps $H\to D$, $x\mapsto(a,x)$ and $x\mapsto(b,x)$ have equal composites with $R$, namely $(\tau_a(x),x)=(\tau_b(x),x)$. Applying $R^{-1}$ gives $(a,x)=(b,x)$ as morphisms on $H$. Thus $a\circ p=b\circ p$ on $H$, where $p:Y_T\to T$. This is cancellation of an actual isomorphism, including its structure sheaf maps, not cancellation only on geometric points.

source.place: 5.2 Lemma 4, cancellation with the universal right translation, printed p.118

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change], $\mathcal O_{Y_T}\to j_*\mathcal O_H$ is injective for $j:H\hookrightarrow Y_T$. The equalizer $E$ of $a\circ p$ and $b\circ p$ is closed: it is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of $Y\to S$. On affine charts this is the ideal generated by the differences of pullbacks of functions on $Y$. All its sections restrict to zero on $H$ by step 3; injectivity of restriction makes that ideal zero. Consequently $E=Y_T$ as a scheme and $a\circ p=b\circ p$ everywhere. No reducedness of $T$ or $Y_T$ is used.

source.place: 5.2 Lemma 4, extension from the dense open, printed p.118; Stacks Tag 01RE (lemma-characterize-scheme-theoretically-dense)

proof.text: The morphism $p:Y_T\to T$ is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and is quasi-compact by its finite type property [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Its nonempty fibres make it surjective. For each affine open $Q\subset T$, a finite affine covering of $p^{-1}(Q)$ therefore maps onto $Q$, so $\{p\}$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Apply uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the common map $a\circ p=b\circ p:Y_T\to Y$. Its two pullbacks agree since it already comes from $a$. Both $a$ and $b$ are descents of it, hence $a=b$. This proves injectivity for every $T$; when $T$ is empty all these maps are the unique empty morphisms.

source.place: 5.2 Lemma 4, final descent to equality of sections; Stacks Tag 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms)

proof.text: To justify specialization of associativity, let $P\subset Y\times_SY$ be any domain representing $m$ by $m_P$. On the open $K\subset Y\times_SY\times_SY$ specified by $(u,v)\in P$, $(v,w)\in D$, $(u,m(v,w))\in D$ and $(m_P(u,v),w)\in D$, both morphisms $F(u,v,w)=m(u,m(v,w))$ and $G(u,v,w)=m(m_P(u,v),w)$ are defined. The triple product is smooth over $S$: its projections are base changes of $Y\to S$ by [lem-sfb-strict-law-base-change], and use [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Its open $K$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Associativity as equality of $S$-rational maps gives an $S$-dense open $C$ in the triple product where these two expressions agree, after intersecting the domains of their representatives. On $C\cap K$ they still agree: the replacement $m_P$ agrees with $m$ on its common domain by the equalizer argument in step 2. The open $C\cap K$ is dense in every fibre of $K$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] it is schematically dense in $K$. The equalizer ideal of $F,G$ (pullback of the closed diagonal of $Y$) is zero by restriction, as in step 4. Hence $F=G$ on all of $K$, before any substitution of $T$-points.

source.place: 5.2 Lemma 4, associativity argument, printed pp.118-119; explicit common-domain justification

proof.text: Now let $(a,b):T\to P$ and $c=m_P(a,b)$. Pull $K$ back along $(a,b,\mathrm{id}_{Y_T})$. Its domain is $J=D_b\cap\tau_b^{-1}(D_a)\cap D_c$, where the inverse image is taken on $D_b$, the domain of $\tau_b$. In each fibre, $\tau_b:D_b\simeq V_b$ is an isomorphism between dense opens, and $V_b\cap D_a$ is dense in $V_b$; thus $D_b\cap\tau_b^{-1}(D_a)$ is dense in $Y_T$. Intersecting with the dense open $D_c$ keeps it dense. The opens $D_a,D_b,D_c,V_b$ have the required fibrewise density by [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] applied to the first projection, as in step 2. Pulling back the actual equality of morphisms $F=G$ from step 6 gives $\tau_a(\tau_b(x))=\tau_c(x)$ on $J$. Equality on this $T$-dense common open is precisely $\tau_a\circ\tau_b=\tau_c$ in $B_Y(T)$. The argument works for every representing domain $P$ and arbitrary, possibly nonreduced, $T$.

source.place: 5.2 Lemma 4, compatibility with composition, printed p.119

The delivery is one commit with the item and the report, has no new nodes, leaves the statement and stmt_deps unchanged, and creates no cycle (485-node closure). Checks: (1) B_Y is a group functor via lem-sfb-strict-law-base-change and the density base-change lemma; composites are taken on U∩f^-1(V∩U'), where the fibrewise homeomorphism keeps them dense. (2) τ_a is the pullback of L:D≅V along a for the smooth pr1. Independence of the representative of m is extended from an S-dense open to all of P∩D by schematic density on the smooth Y×Y and the closed diagonal; this matters because S-density does not give pr1-fibre density. (3) Cancellation through R^-1 on H⊂D_a∩D_b is elementary and correct. (4) Schematic density plus the equalizer ideal gives a∘p=b∘p without assuming T reduced; tested on k[ε]/ε² and T=∅. (5) p is flat, quasi-compact and surjective, so {p} is an fpqc covering, and descent uniqueness gives a=b; the facts that p is smooth with nonempty fibres come from step 1's citation, which is minor. (6) F=G on all of K, because C∩K is S-fibre dense in the smooth K. (7) The pullback domain J=D_b∩τ_b^-1(D_a∩V_b)∩D_c is T-dense, so τ_{m(a,b)}=τ_a∘τ_b in the stated order. BLR is not held locally (WANTED); proof_origin is agent, and the mathematics was checked directly. No duplicate: graph-charts is a citer, and trait-birational-envelope and bounded-group-translation-model state different things. I accept the four tool_uses: all are Mathlib leaves for smoothness permanence and fpqc uniqueness. Batch 5: lem-trf-smooth-composition is the Mathlib leaf for composing smooth morphisms, and lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion (reached through the density lemma) is the generic flat-plus-fibre criterion for smoothness. Neither is a step of the trace formula or of Poincaré duality, so both are accepted.
